# Cedric Stanhope

## Overview

- **Age:** 16 years old by Volume 5  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c18 P28](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0028), [v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004), [v2 c23 P0](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0000), [v2 c27 P4](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0004)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v2 c27 P4](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0004)</sub>
- **Rank:** Student  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v2 c1 P48](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0048)</sub>
- **Role:** Student and aspiring poet  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c24 P16](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0016), [v2 c26 P13](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Cedric has a delicate, refined face surrounded by chestnut curls and striking dark blue eyes. He has a fair complexion, crimson lips, and a smile that lights up his whole face. Though considered small for his age in his younger years, he grows tall by his teens.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004), [v2 c18 P15](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0015), [v2 c27 P4](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0004)_

## Personality

Cedric is an imaginative, sensitive, and grave boy who possesses a deep, poetic soul. Highly intelligent and polite, he is deeply devoted to his family and friends, particularly Nell. Despite his gentle and dreamy disposition, he is manly and able to hold his own among other boys.

_Sources: [v1 c18 P35](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0035), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c5 P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004)_

## Goals

- To become a poet  <sub>[v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>
- To reunite and live permanently with his father  <sub>[v2 c5 P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020)</sub>

## History

Cedric arrived in Brierley to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope, after living in the United States. He enrolled at the Brierley school, where he quickly bonded with the new teacher, Nell Harcourt, recognizing her as a kindred spirit. During a crisis when Posy Fay fell ill with croup, Cedric's quick action in fetching Nell helped save the child's life. He excelled at school and developed a talent for writing poetry. Later, his father Stephen Stanhope visited and eventually rekindled his romance with his former love, Rosalind Penrose. Cedric bonded warmly with Rosalind, accepting her as his stepmother. When Stephen and Rosalind married, plans were made for Cedric to move to Boston with them after his studies.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c18 P21](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0021), [v1 c18 P35](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0035), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c18 P20](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0020), [v2 c19 P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033), [v2 c23 P33](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0033), [v2 c24 P16](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0016), [v2 c29 P11](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0011)_

## Background by volume

- Born in the United States to Stephen Stanhope and his late wife  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v2 c1 P48](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0048), [v2 c5 P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020)</sub>
- Lost his mother at a young age  <sub>[v2 c5 P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020), [v2 c19 P24](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0024)</sub>
- Sent to live with his grandmother in Brierley, St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v2 c1 P48](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0048)</sub>

## Quotes

> I ask you to take these, teacher, which I discovered in the field belonging to Mr. Duckett, and I returned so I could offer them to you since I believed you were a lady who would appreciate them, and also because . . . teacher, I am fond of you.  <sub>[v2 c5 P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020)</sub>

> Do you know what I think? I think an angel walks over the world after the sun sets . . . a great, tall, white angel, with silvery folded wings . . . and sings the flowers and birds to sleep.  <sub>[v2 c11 P43](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0043)</sub>

> Mrs. Sowerby, father made a pretty good job of picking out my first mother and I could trust him to pick out just as good a one the second time.  <sub>[v2 c19 P23](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0023)</sub>

> Teacher, you will never age. You belong to those lucky human beings who discovered and imbibed the Fountain of Youth,—you alongside Mother Rosalind.  <sub>[v2 c24 P3](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0003)</sub>
